title: Estius: charity perfects faith so it merits; one habit is not another's subject
source_text: V. Sic Scholae Romanae mentem explicat Gul. Estius: Non enim, inquit, charitas forma fidei dicitur, quasi ad essentiam fidei pertinens, aut quia fidem proprie informet, cum unus habitus non sit subjectum alterius. Sed hactenus, quia per charitatem aliud, fides perficitur & formatur, ut meritoria sit, & ad aeternam salutem proficiat, quomodo & aliarum omnium virtutum forma charitas appellatur. Ad Distinct. 23. lib. 3. Sententiarum, paragr. 3.
pass_a_gloss: Thus William Estius explains the mind of the Roman School: For charity, he says, is not called the form of faith as if pertaining to the essence of faith, or because it properly informs faith, since one habit is not the subject of another. But thus far, because through charity otherwise, faith is perfected and formed so that it may be meritorious and may profit unto eternal salvation, in the way in which charity is also called the form of all other virtues. On Distinct. 23 of book 3 of the Sentences, paragraph 3.
pass_b_english: Estius: charity is not faith's essential form, and one habit is not another's subject.
Rather, through charity faith is perfected and formed so as to be meritorious and to profit to eternal salvation — as charity is called the form of all other virtues.
